decision.risk_area: public API contracts (onCacheNotAvailable callback now receives a reason string)
decision.why: One module (cache middleware) plus its tests, 138 test files in repo so the change is verifiable; many interacting requirements (key construction, body reading without consuming, size limit, Web Crypto fallback) make it reasoning-heavy, so effort goes up rather than the tier.

checks.reason: In src/middleware/cache/index.ts the QUERY key is still a string, `url + " QUERY body=<hash> content-type=..."`, and it goes to `cache.match`/`cache.put`. The real Cache API turns a string key into a URL and percent-encodes the spaces, so a GET to `/search%20QUERY%20body=<hash>%20content-type=...` gets the same key and serves the cached QUERY entry. It also means custom keys are still resolved as URLs. The test only passes because the Map-backed stub never parses keys. Build a key that a GET URL can't produce, even after URL normalization (for example a different scheme or host, or a key Request built so that no GET request URL maps to it), and don't hand custom keys to URL resolution.

I found no defect. In src/middleware/cache/index.ts, the QUERY cache key includes the method, the base key, a SHA-256 of the body, the four Content-* headers and the Vary values. It is built under a reserved `.invalid` host, which GET requests are never cached for. The body is read from a clone, or from `bodyCache` when an earlier middleware already read it (`json`/`parseBody` go through `text`/`arrayBuffer`). The size limit is inclusive with a 64 KiB default, and unreadable bodies bypass caching. Without Web Crypto, only QUERY bypasses and the callback fires once at creation with the reason string.
